ratification.note: The project owner has opened this bounded C1 acceptance attempt for independent review. The candidate cannot ratify or accept itself; ratification and acceptance remain owned by the post-run governance decision.

acceptance_meaning: Nothing is accepted by this package. It is a C1 candidate that records an implemented, isolated, mandate-scoped WS-04 frontend and the mechanically demonstrated absence of every prohibited capability for independent governed review.

stage_opening.consequence: A bounded FRONT-05 C1 candidate may be sealed and independently reviewed; no acceptance or FRONT-layer closure follows before a successful authoritative run and post-run governance record.
stage_opening.source: Project-owner directive to conduct canonical FRONT-05 verification to PASS, recorded in docs/frontend/FRONT-05-C1-GOVERNANCE-OPENING.json and the candidate Program Control Register.

permitted_before_independent_acceptance: FRONT-05 = OPEN FOR BOUNDED C1 INDEPENDENT REVIEW

route_prefix_reconciliation.disposition: OPEN_GOVERNANCE_ITEM: the accepted frontend policy record carries a display name in the route-prefix field. The architecture source gives /representative. This package uses /representative and records the conflict rather than silently choosing.

implementable_now: isolated WS-04 shell and route set
mandate-scope binding with no expressible cross-mandate form
session and authority state model including expiry, revocation and scope change
case intake and triage presentation contracts
position, deviation and declaration composition contracts

blocked_capability_condition: A capability may be dependency-blocked if and only if the frontend fails closed for it, names its exact missing dependency, and does not simulate it.

hard_invariants.statement: No universal, cross-mandate or administrative mode exists, under any role, permission or debug flag.
Every protected read and action binds to exactly one mandate scope, and no unbound form is expressible.
WS-04 may propose a publication rendition and may never approve one. No approval state is reachable from any client state under any event.
WS-04 holds no registry custody: no registry mutation operation exists.
WS-04 takes no eligibility decision; it may only display one made elsewhere.
WS-04 has no voting-domain access of any kind, for any role.
Case content is never written to browser storage, a URL, the page title, a telemetry event or an error report.
No authoritative decision is taken in the client; a rendered control is never an authorization.
A refusal about a protected resource is non-disclosing: absent, out of scope and restricted are indistinguishable.
An unreadable conflict register restricts rather than permits; unknown is never treated as cleared.
No specification-level or unaccepted API path is treated as an executable runtime route, and no network request is issued from the production adapter.
No success language may precede an authoritative server outcome, and a blocked compliance submission must state that the obligation remains open.
The inherited FRONT-00/FRONT-01 visual baseline is immutable without a Design Change Decision.
Inherited accepted evidence and documents are byte-identical to the accepted bytes they came from.
A recorded PASS is bound to the source tree that produced it; stale evidence must cause a deterministic FAIL.
Every identity value quoted in the developer report equals the corresponding value in the evidence it claims to describe.
A locale change alters no authority, scope, state or legal effect.
No service-to-service credential, private key or bearer authority is present in the browser.
The governed test fixture is absent from the production build, not merely unreachable in it.
This package never asserts its own acceptance.
A capability whose dependency is a security-sensitive boundary is never reported as supported, and no caller-asserted authorization is treated as evidence that authorization occurred.

prohibited_remedies: inventing a representative or mandate API
inventing a publication proposal state on the server's behalf
treating compliance-service RepresentationMandate as an elected mandate
fabricating citizen cases outside the marked governed test profile
reporting a compliance obligation as discharged
regenerating an inherited visual baseline to clear a regression
softening a mutation instead of closing the gate it exposed
treating a caller-supplied actor_is_authorized boolean as evidence of authorization
recording a security-sensitive dependency as a declared limitation rather than a block

report_identity_crosscheck.rule: Every 64-hex digest and every numeric size quoted in the developer report must equal the value recorded in the evidence record it names.
report_identity_crosscheck.rationale: The FRONT-04 C2 archive was rejected and resealed because the developer report quoted a source_tree_digest from a penultimate run while the sealed tree carried another. The report sat outside the digest-covered boundary, so no gate checked it. This contract closes that hole by making the report's own quoted identities a gated artifact.

list.name: security_sensitive_dependency_discipline
list.note: Not in the assignment seed. Added because a caller-supplied actor_is_authorized boolean is a defective authorization boundary rather than a missing feature, and a status vocabulary that offers SUPPORTED_WITH_DECLARED_LIMITATION would otherwise let it be recorded as a limitation.

security_sensitive_dependencies.principle: A dependency that is missing and a dependency that is defective are different findings. A missing dependency becomes a real path when it is built. A defective one must be corrected before it may be relied on at all, and a route appearing over the top of it does not correct it.
security_sensitive_dependencies.rule: A capability whose dependency is classified SECURITY_SENSITIVE_BOUNDARY may only carry status BLOCKED_BY_DEPENDENCY or UNSUPPORTED. It may never be SUPPORTED_REAL_PATH, and it may never be SUPPORTED_WITH_DECLARED_LIMITATION — a declared limitation states the bounds within which something is safe, and there are no bounds within which a self-asserted authorization is safe.

boundaries.observed: Publication has the single state PUBLISHED, and authorization is a caller-supplied actor_is_authorized boolean.
boundaries.finding: A caller-supplied authorization boolean is a self-asserted authorization: the caller declares its own permission and the service accepts the declaration. The field that looks like an authorization gate is an authorization claim, made by exactly the party the gate exists to constrain. Accepting it as sufficient would let a rendition reach publication carrying nothing but the proposer's own claim of being allowed to publish — which is the separation WS-04 exists to preserve.
boundaries.front05_position: FRONT-05 does not treat this boolean as evidence that authorization occurred, does not set or send such a flag, and builds no privileged path on it. No port signature contains a field it could be carried in.
insufficient_remedies: adding a proposal route while authorization stays caller-supplied
treating a successful call as evidence that authorization occurred
boundaries.unblocking_condition: a server-authoritative proposal and authorization contract: a proposal state distinct from PUBLISHED, and an approval decided and recorded by an authority other than the proposer.
boundaries.status_until_then: BLOCKED_BY_DEPENDENCY, with publication approval itself remaining prohibited for WS-04 under every dependency state.
boundaries.escalation: Reported to the accepting authority as a security-relevant finding against PACK-13, not as a FRONT-05 gap.
